The actual formulas are P1=[c]((x+Wc+beta)G_W(x)T(c)/c), x=W(S+a), W=m^2, beta=(W+1)/2. The original fixed-r0 differentiation precedes lambda substitution. With D=W-1, d=W-3, E=lambda partial_lambda, B=b+W-1, tau=(m^4-1)/(24m), g=m tau,

`Psi=C-g(B+2)+alpha[D(D-1)B-(2D-1)EB+E^2B]`,

## 3. Actual carrier, circle and directional support

The actual space has degrees at most m-2 and dimension m-1. The proof temporarily uses the larger degree-at-most N=m-1 Student space only to obtain upper bounds. For f_s=(v-i/2)^s(v+i/2)^(N-s), the product |f_s|^2 w_m equals `4^(-N)/(1+4v^2)`. The ratio y=(v-i/2)/(v+i/2) parametrizes the unit circle once with constant angle measure after this weight, so the f_s are mutually orthogonal with a common norm. This is an explicit positive auxiliary form, not positivity of the original finite-rho Gram metric.

All f_s are monic of degree N, hence the old carrier is precisely the hyperplane sum a_s=0. Differentiation preserves it. I differentiated the displayed basis directly and recovered

`D_v f_s=-i s f_(s-1)+i(2s-N)f_s+i(N-s)f_(s+1)`.

The absolute row and column sums are bounded by 2m. For Re(e^(i theta)D_v), the real diagonal is (N-2s)sin theta, and the adjacent entry is `(2s-m)sin(theta)/2-i m cos(theta)/2`. Its modulus is at most m/2, so Hermitian row sums give `||Re(e^(i theta)D_v)||<=m(1+|sin theta|)`. Compression to the invariant actual space preserves this numerical-range estimate; the actual adjoint is the compressed adjoint. Conjugating the direction gives the corresponding adjoint estimate. Thus (9) holds without normality or a diagonalizable spectral model.

The old reflection compatibility is used coefficient by coefficient. Z0 and every even derivative coefficient commute with reflection. Consequently Z^sharp at a complex lambda is `(Z_(conjugate lambda))^dagger`, and is holomorphic in lambda. Replacing it silently by Z_lambda^dagger would be wrong; the manuscript does not do that. The old even compressed multiplier has ||A_e||<=4. The cutoff n is the largest even integer <=m-2. Z and R have degree at most n-1 and b,C,Eb,E^2b have degree at most q=2n-2<=2m-6<d. Both parity choices of m and the codimension-one exclusion are preserved.

## 4. Fourier sign, resolvent and thick-domain estimates

The unchanged selected NIST 24.8.1 even Bernoulli Fourier identity is valid for n=1,2,... and 0<=x<=1, including x=0. Combined with J=-i D_v and the actual even nilpotent cutoff it gives the minus coefficients in (5). I reused my prior complete read of the shared official 122-byte selected TeX and selected page/domain and HTTP records. Retrieval owner remains 7CDA; I do not claim a new personal HTTP retrieval or whole-chapter reading. Exact hashes and read scopes are in the context.

Expanding each factor in (10) in the nilpotent D_v recovers exactly `-2 zeta(k) lambda^(k-1)D_v^k/(2pi)^k` for each permitted even k. This checks the real-pole sign. Every inverse is a finite polynomial; the h-sum is justified coefficientwise and also admits the displayed convergent uniform norm majorant. Finite polynomiality is not a claim that the sufficient numerical-range domain is unnecessary for its bound.

For m>=100, m xi<=6m^2/(m^2-3)<6.1. On the larger 1/(100m) neighborhood, `m(|lambda|+|Im lambda|)<6.12`. Thus the real parts of `I +/- lambda D_v/(2pi h)` are bounded below by `1-6.12/(2pi h)`, uniformly greater than 1/64 using 2pi>6.28. The elementary accretive inverse estimate is valid on the actual finite Hilbert space and needs no normality. The same holds for D_v^dagger.

Factoring the quadratic inverse, applying the two inverse bounds, ||D_v||<=2m, |lambda|<7/m and sum h^-2<2 gives the correction bound `(114688/9)m`. Adding ||Z0||<=2m is less than 2^14m. The coefficientwise-adjoint formula obeys the same bound. Hence ||R||<=2^15m and |b|<=2^30m^3. The commutator and both C traces, with dimension<=m and ||A_e||<=4, give the stated deliberately loose |C|<=2^34m^6.

Disks of radius 1/(200m) centered in the smaller neighborhood lie in the larger one. Cauchy gives |b'|<=200m*2^30m^3 and |b''|<=2(200m)^2*2^30m^3. Multiplying by |lambda|<7/m and using `E^2b=lambda b'+lambda^2 b''` verifies |Eb|<=2^41m^3 and |E^2b|<=2^53m^3 throughout the required domain. These are holomorphic coefficientwise derivatives, not derivatives of a moving positive Hermitian form.

## 5. Exact functional, contour and binomial normalization

For degree at most d, `(1+z)^d p(z/(1+z))` is a polynomial, and monomial extraction proves its z^j coefficient is binom(d,j)Lp. Under z=lambda/(1-lambda), `dz/z=d lambda/[lambda(1-lambda)]`. I recovered (13), including P_j=binom(d,j)xi^j(1-xi)^(d-j), both powers in the normalized kernel, and the extra factor 1/(1-lambda) in the measure.

The radial contour is simple, piecewise C1, positively winds once around zero, and stays in |lambda|<1. Its corner points cause no integral problem. Thus the transformed extraction is exact. It is not a saddle-point approximation, a Gaussian substitution, or an eta-weight truncation.

For theta in [0,pi], h=cos(theta)/(1+sin(theta)), F=h-1+log(1+sin(theta)), and direct differentiation gives `F'=(cos(theta)-1)/(1+sin(theta))`. Since 1-cos(theta)>=2theta^2/pi^2 and pi^2<10, F'<=-theta^2/10 and F<=-theta^3/30.

I checked the cancellation in the log-kernel estimate: keeping `log(1-xi)<=-xi-xi^2/2` and bounding the remaining complex series by `Re lambda+|lambda|^2/[2(1-|lambda|)]` leaves at most xi^3/[2(1-xi)]. After multiplication by d-j this is exactly j xi^2/2. The linear remainder is j(h-1)+j xi(1-h), with 0<=1-h<=2. Hence the logarithmic modulus is at most `jF+(5/2)jxi`; at m>=100 and j<=6m the latter addition is below 100. This establishes the e^100 cubic majorant on both arcs, without dropping the unfavorable quadratic contribution.

The logarithmic derivative of the radial contour has modulus at most sqrt(2) almost everywhere; together with xi<0.061 this implies the claimed measure bound 3 dtheta. For the binomial normalization, floor((d+1)xi)=j, so P_j is a maximum mass. Chebyshev puts at least 3/4 of the finite mass in an interval with at most 5sqrt(j) integers. Thus P_j>=3/(20sqrt(j))>1/(8sqrt(j)), proving the stated weaker (16). No sampled or asymptotic mass estimate is used.

## 6. Subtraction and the uniform quantitative transfer

The functional preserves 1 and lambda exactly. Subtracting the constant and first Taylor terms therefore leaves precisely the difference in (2). For |theta|<=1/10000, the contour displacement obeys `|lambda-xi|<=14|theta|/m`; relative to the available 1/(200m) disk its modulus is at most 0.28. Cauchy coefficients and the geometric Taylor tail then give (17), with substantial slack in 2^40.

Outside this arc, the two point values are each bounded by Hm^r, the derivative by 200Hm^(r+1), and displacement by 14/m. Their sum is at most 2802Hm^r; since theta^2>=10^-8, this too is below 2^40Hm^r theta^2. This argument uses the specified complex neighborhood, not a real-axis norm or an arbitrary similarity condition number.

Finally the exact integral `integral_0^pi theta^2 exp(-jtheta^3/30) dtheta <=10/j`, the two arcs, the measure estimate and P_j bound give the manuscript's looser `120*2^40 e^100 Hm^r/sqrt(j)`. Using e<4 and j>=4m makes this less than 2^246Hm^(r-1/2), hence certainly the claimed 2^250 bound. This proves the full polynomial-family statement with its given quantifiers. The known negative value of L((lambda-xi)^2) is consistent with it: such positivity is never asserted, and the norm hypothesis has not been removed.

## 7. Whole-Psi transfer, constants and effective threshold

For real xi, R is the actual Hermitian sum. Z is degree-triangular with the old diagonal k-m+1/2 for k=0,...,m-2. Thus tr R=-(m^2-1). Cauchy-Schwarz for its m-1 real eigenvalues gives `b(xi)>m^3`, exactly (18). The application does not infer coefficient positivity from this evaluation; it uses the proved transfer bound.

For b, H=2^30,r=3 gives error at most 2^280m^(5/2). At m>=2^1000 it is less than m^3/2. For Eb,E^2b the transfer errors are at most 2^291m^(5/2) and 2^303m^(5/2); relative to their respective evaluation bounds, the doubled bounds in (19) only need m^(1/2)>=2^250. Likewise C has H=2^34,r=6, and B+2 has H=2^31,r=3, retaining the positive scalar W+1. All of these conditions are weaker than the chosen uniform threshold. Their polynomial degrees satisfy q<d, so the same exact functional applies.

The leading contribution is at least `(m^2/8)(m^4/2)(m^3/2)=m^9/32`. The additional positive W-1 in B helps this term and is constant under E. Using alpha<=m^2 and g<=m^4, the adverse first-derivative term is at most 2^43m^7, the second-derivative term at most 2^54m^5, C at most 2^35m^6, and g(B+2) at most 2^32m^7. Their sum is bounded by 2^56m^7, which is at most m^9/64 at the declared threshold. Consequently `L Psi>=m^9/64`. Multiplication by the unchanged positive K binom(d,j) proves the exact raw-coefficient bound.

This explicitly accounts for the C commutator and its linear term, both Euler derivatives and their signs, the W+1 scalar, and the old factor m^2 in alpha. There is no omission of a centered-to-raw correction, replacement by a positive-square functional, extension from a low-m matrix, or passage from a sampled m to all m.
